ranked_evidence.title: The 2026 Fields Medals Are Awarded To Four Young Mathematicians - Forbes
ranked_evidence.snippet: # The 2026 Fields Medals Are Awarded To Four Young Mathematicians. The prestigious Fields Medals, often called the Nobel Prize of mathematics, were awarded to four distinguished mathematicians at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Philadelphia on July 23. Yu Deng (University of Chicago), Jacob Tsimerman (University of Toronto), Hong Wang (NYU/IHES), and John Pardon (Stony Brook University) received the honor. Awarded every four years to mathematicians under 40, the medal recognizes outstanding achievement and future promise. The four winners of the 2026 Fields Medal, often considered to be the equivalent of the Nobel Prize in the field of mathematics, have been named by the International Mathematical Union (IMU). The Fields Medal is awarded every four years to two to four mathematicians who are younger than the age of 40. “The four medalists exemplify the depth, originality and vitality of contemporary mathematics, and we are delighted to celebrate their achievements at the International Congress of Mathematicians,” said Hiraku Nakajima, president of the IMU, in a statement.

ranked_evidence.title: Delhi Government Replaces 'Essentiality Certificate' With Self-Certifications - NDTV
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Delhi Government Replaces 'Essentiality Certificate' With Self-Certifications. ## New rules align Delhi's school recognition with RTE Act, focusing on infrastructure, teacher qualifications, and safety standards. Delhi introduces self-certification in place of Essentiality Certificate for private schools. * Delhi replaces Essentiality Certificate with self-certification for private schools. * New rules align with RTE Act focusing on infrastructure and teacher standards. The Delhi government has approved a major change in the process for opening private schools by replacing the long-standing 'Essentiality Certificate' requirement with a self-certification system. According to ANI, Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood has approved the reform, under which the Directorate of Education will remove several outdated provisions under the Delhi School Education Act and Rules (DSER), 1973. Under the new system, private schools will no longer have to obtain an Essentiality Certificate, which earlier required government approval on whether a new school was needed in a particular area.

ranked_evidence.title: Olivia Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields Etsy Merch Proves Festival Fashion Is So Back - Teen Vogue
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Olivia Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields Etsy Merch Is the Perfect Blend of Cottagecore and Whimsy. Olivia Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields music festival is rapidly approaching, and to celebrate, she's launching a merch collab with Etsy that's full of daisy motifs, vintage vibes, and a whimsical floral spirit. The official Daisy Chain Fields Collection by Olivia Rodrigo is a curated, handmade collection from 10 female-owned Etsy shops, and is available exclusively on the platform starting today, July 23. It's a fun way to do festival merch—highlighting both the women-centric vibe of the festival (which is already being compared to the groundbreaking Lilith Fair) and Rodrigo's personal approach to its curation. The Etsy Creative Village will also be available on-site at the music festival on Aug. 29 at Great Park in Irvine, California; at the pop-up, “many of those same Etsy sellers will bring the collaboration to life through hands-on creative experiences, festival exclusives and opportunities for fans to meet the makers,” according to a press release.

ranked_evidence.title: From Banana Farms to Makhana Markets: The Highway Set to Power Bihar’s Agricultural Heartland - Global Agriculture
ranked_evidence.snippet: Home » India Region » From Banana Farms to Makhana Markets: The Highway Set to Power Bihar’s Agricultural Heartland. # From Banana Farms to Makhana Markets: The Highway Set to Power Bihar’s Agricultural Heartland. ****20** July 2026, **New Delhi**:** Before dawn breaks over the fertile plains of Bihar, trucks loaded with bunches of bananas leave the farms of Khagaria, while sacks of makhana begin their journey from ponds and processing centres of Purnea, one of the country’s biggest makhana hubs. The proposed upgradation of the Khagaria–Purnea section of NH-31 and NH-231 to a four-lane highway by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, recently approved by Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), seeks to address these longstanding challenges. The upgradation of the Khagaria-Purnea Section of NH-31 and NH-231 to 4-lane standard in Bihar at a cost of Rs.3936.05 crore is more of an investment in the people whose livelihoods depend on getting Bihar’s bananas and makhana to market efficiently, helping strengthen the economic backbone of the state’s agricultural heartland.

ranked_evidence.snippet: In case you want to opt out, please click "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information" link in the footer of this page. ## The government has extended the exemption for net-metering and open access RE projects. New Delhi, The government on Saturday said it has extended the exemption timeline for net-metering and open access RE projects till December 31, 2026 under the ALMM-II. In a statement, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy said there is no change in ALMM Policy and the government has provided extended relief window for select solar projects up to December 2026. The MNRE has decided that there will be no change in the policy of the Government of India with respect of implementation of Approved List of Models & Manufacturers (ALMM) List-II for solar PV cells, and no blanket extension in applicability of ALMM List-II for solar power projects will be provided.

ranked_evidence.title: ICAR @98: Science, innovation and sustainability for Viksit Bharat 2047 - The Economic Times
ranked_evidence.snippet: In case you want to opt out, please click "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information" link in the footer of this page. As the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) marks its 98th Foundation Day, the occasion celebrates the remarkable journey of the country’s premier agricultural research, education, and extension organisation, while highlighting its enduring commitment to transforming Indian agriculture through farmer-centric technologies, science, innovation, and last-mile delivery. Over the past nine+ decades, ICAR has played a pivotal role in ensuring India’s food, nutrition, and livelihood security by continuously developing and disseminating climate-resilient crop varieties, better livestock breeds, sustainable natural resource management practices, and scale-appropriate farming tools. Today, as India advances towards the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047, agriculture remains central to economic growth, environmental sustainability, and rural prosperity. The next phase of India’s agricultural transformation must, therefore, be driven by scientific excellence, technological innovation, and a calibrated transition towards a sustainable bioeconomy.
